texts.facts: Hence, no process fee is required to be paid for issuance of notice to this Respondents.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the proceedings of sealing the hotel of the petitioner on 30.08.2024 is as a counter blast of the execution proceedings filed by the petitioner arising out of the judgment and decree passed in the civil suit filed by him for recovery of the sum of Rs. 24,50,159/-. He contended that the Executing Court has passed an order on 26.07.2024 for issuing Kurki warrant and the date fixed for the report of the Kurki warrant was 30.08.2024. It is clearly appearing that as soon as the person approached the government office for service of the Kurki Warrant, immediately thereafter, in the night at about 08:30 P.M., all the officials of the departments of State administration reached to the hotel and by recording the panchnama in a cryptic manner; has sealed the entire hotel and restaurant. Learned counsel for the petitioner further contended that no specific reason has been assigned of violation of any of the provisions of the National Food Security and Standards Act, 2006 or the Chhattisgarh Excise Act, 1915 in a specific manner. He also submits that after sealing of the premises of the hotel and restaurant, subsequently, thereafter, show-cause notices have been issued on 03.09.2024 and 04.09.202. The action of the sealing has been done prior to the issuance of notice and submission of the reply. The entire business of the petitioner has been closed and therefore, till the respondents file reply, direction be issued for unsealing of the hotel. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respective respondents opposes the submission of the counsel for the petitioner and would submit that from the Panchnama (Ex. P/8), it is appearing that the officials of the State Government who visited the hotel of the petitioner found irregularities and also use of expiry products and therefore, petitioner is not entitled for any interim relief.
